فَٱلْحَٰمِلَٰتِ وِقْرًا
فَٱلْجَٰرِيَٰتِ يُسْرًا
فَٱلْمُقَسِّمَٰتِ أَمْرًا
إِنَّمَا تُوعَدُونَ لَصَادِقٌ
وَإِنَّ ٱلدِّينَ لَوَٰقِعٌ
وَٱلسَّمَآءِ ذَاتِ ٱلْحُبُكِ
إِنَّكُمْ لَفِى قَوْلٍ مُّخْتَلِفٍ
يُؤْفَكُ عَنْهُ مَنْ أُفِكَ
قُتِلَ ٱلْخَرَّٰصُونَ
ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ فِى غَمْرَةٍ سَاهُونَ
يَسْـَٔلُونَ أَيَّانَ يَوْمُ ٱلدِّينِ
يَوْمَ هُمْ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ يُفْتَنُونَ
ذُوقُوا۟ فِتْنَتَكُمْ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِى كُنتُم بِهِۦ تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ
إِنَّ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ فِى جَنَّٰتٍ وَعُيُونٍ
ءَاخِذِينَ مَآ ءَاتَىٰهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَبْلَ ذَٰلِكَ مُحْسِنِينَ
كَانُوا۟ قَلِيلًا مِّنَ ٱلَّيْلِ مَا يَهْجَعُونَ
وَبِٱلْأَسْحَارِ هُمْ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ
وَفِىٓ أَمْوَٰلِهِمْ حَقٌّ لِّلسَّآئِلِ وَٱلْمَحْرُومِ
وَفِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ءَايَٰتٌ لِّلْمُوقِنِينَ
وَفِىٓ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَفَلَا تُبْصِرُونَ
وَفِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ رِزْقُكُمْ وَمَا تُوعَدُونَ
فَوَرَبِّ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ إِنَّهُۥ لَحَقٌّ مِّثْلَ مَآ أَنَّكُمْ تَنطِقُونَ
هَلْ أَتَىٰكَ حَدِيثُ ضَيْفِ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ ٱلْمُكْرَمِينَ
إِذْ دَخَلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِ فَقَالُوا۟ سَلَٰمًا قَالَ سَلَٰمٌ قَوْمٌ مُّنكَرُونَ
فَرَاغَ إِلَىٰٓ أَهْلِهِۦ فَجَآءَ بِعِجْلٍ سَمِينٍ
فَقَرَّبَهُۥٓ إِلَيْهِمْ قَالَ أَلَا تَأْكُلُونَ
فَأَوْجَسَ مِنْهُمْ خِيفَةً قَالُوا۟ لَا تَخَفْ وَبَشَّرُوهُ بِغُلَٰمٍ عَلِيمٍ
فَأَقْبَلَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُهُۥ فِى صَرَّةٍ فَصَكَّتْ وَجْهَهَا وَقَالَتْ عَجُوزٌ عَقِيمٌ
قَالُوا۟ كَذَٰلِكِ قَالَ رَبُّكِ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْحَكِيمُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ
قَالَ فَمَا خَطْبُكُمْ أَيُّهَا ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ
قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّآ أُرْسِلْنَآ إِلَىٰ قَوْمٍ مُّجْرِمِينَ
لِنُرْسِلَ عَلَيْهِمْ حِجَارَةً مِّن طِينٍ
مُّسَوَّمَةً عِندَ رَبِّكَ لِلْمُسْرِفِينَ
فَأَخْرَجْنَا مَن كَانَ فِيهَا مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
فَمَا وَجَدْنَا فِيهَا غَيْرَ بَيْتٍ مِّنَ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ
وَتَرَكْنَا فِيهَآ ءَايَةً لِّلَّذِينَ يَخَافُونَ ٱلْعَذَابَ ٱلْأَلِيمَ
وَفِى مُوسَىٰٓ إِذْ أَرْسَلْنَٰهُ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ بِسُلْطَٰنٍ مُّبِينٍ
فَتَوَلَّىٰ بِرُكْنِهِۦ وَقَالَ سَٰحِرٌ أَوْ مَجْنُونٌ
فَأَخَذْنَٰهُ وَجُنُودَهُۥ فَنَبَذْنَٰهُمْ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌ
وَفِى عَادٍ إِذْ أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلرِّيحَ ٱلْعَقِيمَ
مَا تَذَرُ مِن شَىْءٍ أَتَتْ عَلَيْهِ إِلَّا جَعَلَتْهُ كَٱلرَّمِيمِ
وَفِى ثَمُودَ إِذْ قِيلَ لَهُمْ تَمَتَّعُوا۟ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍ
فَعَتَوْا۟ عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّهِمْ فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ ٱلصَّٰعِقَةُ وَهُمْ يَنظُرُونَ
فَمَا ٱسْتَطَٰعُوا۟ مِن قِيَامٍ وَمَا كَانُوا۟ مُنتَصِرِينَ
وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ مِّن قَبْلُ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ قَوْمًا فَٰسِقِينَ
وَٱلسَّمَآءَ بَنَيْنَٰهَا بِأَيْي۟دٍ وَإِنَّا لَمُوسِعُونَ
وَٱلْأَرْضَ فَرَشْنَٰهَا فَنِعْمَ ٱلْمَٰهِدُونَ
وَمِن كُلِّ شَىْءٍ خَلَقْنَا زَوْجَيْنِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ
فَفِرُّوٓا۟ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ إِنِّى لَكُم مِّنْهُ نَذِيرٌ مُّبِينٌ
وَلَا تَجْعَلُوا۟ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَ إِنِّى لَكُم مِّنْهُ نَذِيرٌ مُّبِينٌ
كَذَٰلِكَ مَآ أَتَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِم مِّن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا قَالُوا۟ سَاحِرٌ أَوْ مَجْنُونٌ
أَتَوَاصَوْا۟ بِهِۦ بَلْ هُمْ قَوْمٌ طَاغُونَ
فَتَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ فَمَآ أَنتَ بِمَلُومٍ
وَذَكِّرْ فَإِنَّ ٱلذِّكْرَىٰ تَنفَعُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
وَمَا خَلَقْتُ ٱلْجِنَّ وَٱلْإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُونِ
مَآ أُرِيدُ مِنْهُم مِّن رِّزْقٍ وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَن يُطْعِمُونِ
إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلرَّزَّاقُ ذُو ٱلْقُوَّةِ ٱلْمَتِينُ
فَإِنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ ذَنُوبًا مِّثْلَ ذَنُوبِ أَصْحَٰبِهِمْ فَلَا يَسْتَعْجِلُونِ
فَوَيْلٌ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِن يَوْمِهِمُ ٱلَّذِى يُوعَدُونَ

leads.title: The Shunammite woman and her son ↔ Abraham's honored guests, the barren old wife striking her face, the stones of clay for Lot's people; Pharaoh, 'Ad, Thamud and Noah
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: A barren wife is told by a divine messenger that she will bear a son (weight 5.8); A divine messenger announces a son's birth and gives his name (weight 5.2); Host runs to welcome strangers, washes their feet and feeds them (weight 5.1). Pair score 16.0.

Only in The Shunammite woman and her son: Child in the harvest field cries 'My head, my head!' and dies at noon on his mother's knees; Woman protests the promise of a son: 'Do not lie to your maidservant'; Prophet admits 'YHWH has hidden it from me and not told me'; A wealthy woman has a small roof-chamber built for the holy man with bed, table, chair and lamp; Offered a favor with king or general, the hostess replies 'I dwell among my own people'; Mother lays her dead son on the prophet's bed, shuts the door and rides to fetch him; Husband asks why she visits the prophet when it is neither new moon nor sabbath; Prophet lies on the child, mouth to mouth, eyes to eyes, hands to hands, until the body warms; Servant lays the prophet's staff on the dead child's face but there is no voice or response; Revived child sneezes seven times and opens his eyes; Servant sent in haste must greet no one and answer no greeting on the road; Bereaved woman grasps the prophet's feet; the servant tries to push her away; and 5 more.

Only in Abraham's honored guests, the barren old wife striking her face, the stones of clay for Lot's people; Pharaoh, 'Ad, Thamud and Noah: On 'Ad God sent the barren wind (al-rih al-'aqim), which left everything like rotten bones; Abraham brings a fattened calf but the guests do not eat, and he becomes afraid of them; The honored guests enter saying 'Peace' and Abraham replies 'Peace, strangers (qawm munkarun)'; The guests announce to Abraham a knowing (or wise) son ('alim); Thamud were told 'Enjoy yourselves for a while', defied the command and were seized by the thunderbolt while they looked on; Abraham's wife comes forward crying out, strikes her face and says 'A barren old woman!'; Angels seize the hesitating family by the hand and lead them out; The answer given to the old woman's doubt [divergence between the texts]; Heavenly visitors eat a human meal; Host runs to welcome strangers, washes their feet and feeds them [divergence between the texts]; How Abraham learns of Sodom's fate, and his response [divergence between the texts]; Who Abraham's visitors are [divergence between the texts]; and 17 more.

leads.title: Blessings and the great curses ↔ Al-Dhariyat: the oath by the winds, the conjecturers, the night-wakeful righteous and the beggar's due

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: In heaven is your provision and what you are promised (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in Blessings and the great curses: Futility curse: betroth a wife another lies with, build a house and not live in it, plant a vineyard and not enjoy it; Blessed in city and field, in coming in and going out, basket and kneading trough; Smitten with the boils of Egypt, tumors, scab and itch that cannot be healed; Covenant at Moab in addition to the covenant at Horeb; Delicate woman who never set foot on the ground secretly eats her afterbirth and children in the siege; Enemies come out one way and flee seven ways; King and people exiled to an unknown nation to serve gods of wood and stone; As God rejoiced to do you good, so he will rejoice to destroy you; God will make you the head and not the tail; God puts an iron yoke on your neck; In the morning you will say: would it were evening; in the evening: would it were morning; God will send you back to Egypt in ships to be sold as slaves, and no one will buy; and 20 more.

Only in Al-Dhariyat: the oath by the winds, the conjecturers, the night-wakeful righteous and the beggar's due: God swears by the Lord of heaven and earth that it is as true as the fact that you speak; Oath 'By the sky with its tracks/weaves (dhat al-hubuk)'; 'Perish the conjecturers (al-kharrasun)' who are heedless in a flood of ignorance; In the wealth of the righteous is a known right (haqq ma'lum) for the beggar and the deprived; Oath cluster by the scatterers, the burden-bearers, the easy runners and the distributors of command (winds, clouds, ships or angels); The share of the poor in the owner's harvest or wealth [divergence between the texts]; In the earth are signs for the certain, and in yourselves; will you not see?; Corners of the field, gleanings and fallen grapes left for the poor and the stranger; The righteous slept little of the night and sought forgiveness in the hours before dawn (ashar); Speaker rises at midnight to give thanks to God.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).

matches.label: How Abraham learns of Sodom's fate, and his response
matches.note: How Abraham learns of Sodom's fate, and what follows. Genesis: YHWH decides ha-mḵasseh ʾănî mē-ʾaḇrāhām and tells him of the outcry (zaʿăqaṯ səḏōm), and Abraham bargains for the city (18:23-32). Quran: Abraham asks fa-mā khaṭbukum ayyuhā l-mursalūn and they answer innā ursilnā ilā qawmin mujrimīn; no bargaining in Q 51 (cf. Q 11:74, yujādilunā). God's confidence becomes Abraham's question, and the plea for the city is left out.

matches.label: Who Abraham's visitors are
matches.note: Who the visitors are. Genesis: wa-yērāʾ ʾēlâw YHWH bə-ʾēlōnê mamrēʾ ... wə-hinnēh šəlōšâ ʾănāšîm (YHWH appears, as three men; YHWH himself speaks in 18:13). Quran: ḍayfu ibrāhīma l-mukramīn, addressed as ayyuhā l-mursalūn (51:31): honored guests who are 'sent ones', no number, and God is not among them.

passages.text: וַיֵּרָ֤א אֵלָיו֙ יְהוָ֔ה בְּאֵלֹנֵ֖י מַמְרֵ֑א וְה֛וּא יֹשֵׁ֥ב פֶּֽתַח הָאֹ֖הֶל כְּחֹ֥ם הַיּֽוֹם
וַיִּשָּׂ֤א עֵינָיו֙ וַיַּ֔רְא וְהִנֵּה֙ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה אֲנָשִׁ֔ים נִצָּבִ֖ים עָלָ֑יו וַיַּ֗רְא וַיָּ֤רָץ לִקְרָאתָם֙ מִפֶּ֣תַח הָאֹ֔הֶל וַיִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ אָֽרְצָה
هَلْ أَتَىٰكَ حَدِيثُ ضَيْفِ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ ٱلْمُكْرَمِينَ
قَالَ فَمَا خَطْبُكُمْ أَيُّهَا ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ

matches.label: Host runs to welcome strangers, washes their feet and feeds them
matches.note: The welcome. Genesis: Abraham runs to meet them (wa-yyāroṣ liqrāʾṯām), bows to the ground and begs ʾăḏōnāy ʾim nāʾ māṣāʾṯî ḥēn bə-ʿênêḵā, then wa-yəmahēr ʾaḇrāhām hā-ʾōhĕlâ ʾel śārâ. Quran: the guests speak first, fa-qālū salāman qāla salāmun qawmun munkarūn (Abraham returns the greeting and finds them strange), then fa-rāgha ilā ahlihi (he slipped off to his household). Same hurried move to the tent; the bow and the plea are absent, and Abraham's unease (munkarūn) is added.

passages.text: וַיִּשָּׂ֤א עֵינָיו֙ וַיַּ֔רְא וְהִנֵּה֙ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה אֲנָשִׁ֔ים נִצָּבִ֖ים עָלָ֑יו וַיַּ֗רְא וַיָּ֤רָץ לִקְרָאתָם֙ מִפֶּ֣תַח הָאֹ֔הֶל וַיִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ אָֽרְצָה
וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אֲדֹנָ֗י אִם נָ֨א מָצָ֤אתִי חֵן֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ אַל נָ֥א תַעֲבֹ֖ר מֵעַ֥ל עַבְדֶּֽךָ
וַיְמַהֵ֧ר אַבְרָהָ֛ם הָאֹ֖הֱלָה אֶל שָׂרָ֑ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר מַהֲרִ֞י שְׁלֹ֤שׁ סְאִים֙ קֶ֣מַח סֹ֔לֶת ל֖וּשִׁי וַעֲשִׂ֥י עֻגֽוֹת
إِذْ دَخَلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِ فَقَالُوا۟ سَلَٰمًا قَالَ سَلَٰمٌ قَوْمٌ مُّنكَرُونَ
فَرَاغَ إِلَىٰٓ أَهْلِهِۦ فَجَآءَ بِعِجْلٍ سَمِينٍ

matches.label: Whether Abraham's heavenly guests eat the meal
matches.note: Reversal: in Genesis the visitors eat: wə-hûʾ ʿōmēḏ ʿălêhem taḥaṯ hā-ʿēṣ wa-yyōʾḵēlû. In the Quran they do not: qāla a-lā taʾkulūn, fa-awjasa minhum khīfatan, qālū lā takhaf. The refusal to eat reveals that they are angels and frightens Abraham. cf. Tob 12:19, Gen. Rab. 48:14 and b. Bava Metzia 86b (the angels only seemed to eat), a solution to the same problem; not in the HB.

passages.text: וַיִּקַּ֨ח חֶמְאָ֜ה וְחָלָ֗ב וּבֶן הַבָּקָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וַיִּתֵּ֖ן לִפְנֵיהֶ֑ם וְהֽוּא עֹמֵ֧ד עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם תַּ֥חַת הָעֵ֖ץ וַיֹּאכֵֽלוּ
فَقَرَّبَهُۥٓ إِلَيْهِمْ قَالَ أَلَا تَأْكُلُونَ
فَأَوْجَسَ مِنْهُمْ خِيفَةً قَالُوا۟ لَا تَخَفْ وَبَشَّرُوهُ بِغُلَٰمٍ عَلِيمٍ

matches.label: Sarah's reaction to the announcement of a son
matches.note: Sarah's reaction, changed from inner laughter to an open cry. Genesis: wat-tiṣḥaq śārâ bə-qirbāh lēʾmōr ʾaḥărê ḇəlōṯî ... wa-ʾḏōnî zāqēn; God asks lāmmâ zeh ṣāḥăqâ śārâ and she denies it out of fear (lōʾ ṣāḥaqtî kî yārēʾâ). Quran: fa-aqbalati mraʾatuhu fī ṣarratin fa-ṣakkat wajhahā wa-qālat ʿajūzun ʿaqīm (she came forward crying out, struck her face and said 'a barren old woman!'). The messengers answer ka-dhālika qāla rabbuki innahu huwa l-ḥakīmu l-ʿalīm: no rebuke, no denial, no laughter (ṣ-ḥ-q, the pun on Isaac's name, is gone).

passages.text: וַתִּצְחַ֥ק שָׂרָ֖ה בְּקִרְבָּ֣הּ לֵאמֹ֑ר אַחֲרֵ֤י בְלֹתִי֙ הָֽיְתָה לִּ֣י עֶדְנָ֔ה וַֽאדֹנִ֖י זָקֵֽן
וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל אַבְרָהָ֑ם לָ֣מָּה זֶּה֩ צָחֲקָ֨ה שָׂרָ֜ה לֵאמֹ֗ר הַאַ֥ף אֻמְנָ֛ם אֵלֵ֖ד וַאֲנִ֥י זָקַֽנְתִּי
וַתְּכַחֵ֨שׁ שָׂרָ֧ה לֵאמֹ֛ר לֹ֥א צָחַ֖קְתִּי כִּ֣י יָרֵ֑אָה וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לֹ֖א כִּ֥י צָחָֽקְתְּ
فَأَقْبَلَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُهُۥ فِى صَرَّةٍ فَصَكَّتْ وَجْهَهَا وَقَالَتْ عَجُوزٌ عَقِيمٌ
قَالُوا۟ كَذَٰلِكِ قَالَ رَبُّكِ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْحَكِيمُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ

matches.label: The answer given to the old woman's doubt
matches.note: The answer to the old woman's doubt: hă-yippālēʾ mē-YHWH dāḇār (is anything too wondrous for YHWH?, a rhetorical question by YHWH himself) vs. ka-dhālika qāla rabbuki innahu huwa l-ḥakīmu l-ʿalīm (thus said your Lord; he is the Wise, the Knowing, said by the messengers). Divine power becomes divine wisdom and knowledge, and the speaker is the angels quoting God.

passages.text: הֲיִפָּלֵ֥א מֵיְהוָ֖ה דָּבָ֑ר לַמּוֹעֵ֞ד אָשׁ֥וּב אֵלֶ֛יךָ כָּעֵ֥ת חַיָּ֖ה וּלְשָׂרָ֥ה בֵֽן
قَالُوا۟ كَذَٰلِكِ قَالَ رَبُّكِ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْحَكِيمُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ

matches.label: A tender calf is slaughtered and served to divine guests
matches.note: wa-yiqqaḥ ben bāqār raḵ wā-ṭôḇ ... wa-yiqqaḥ ḥemʾâ wə-ḥālāḇ û-ḇen hab-bāqār ... wa-yittēn lip̄nêhem vs. fa-jāʾa bi-ʿijlin samīnin fa-qarrabahu ilayhim. Genesis: a tender, good calf with curds and milk; Quran: a fat calf only.

passages.text: וְאֶל הַבָּקָ֖ר רָ֣ץ אַבְרָהָ֑ם וַיִּקַּ֨ח בֶּן בָּקָ֜ר רַ֤ךְ וָטוֹב֙ וַיִּתֵּ֣ן אֶל הַנַּ֔עַר וַיְמַהֵ֖ר לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת אֹתֽוֹ
וַיִּקַּ֨ח חֶמְאָ֜ה וְחָלָ֗ב וּבֶן הַבָּקָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וַיִּתֵּ֖ן לִפְנֵיהֶ֑ם וְהֽוּא עֹמֵ֧ד עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם תַּ֥חַת הָעֵ֖ץ וַיֹּאכֵֽלוּ
فَرَاغَ إِلَىٰٓ أَهْلِهِۦ فَجَآءَ بِعِجْلٍ سَمِينٍ
فَقَرَّبَهُۥٓ إِلَيْهِمْ قَالَ أَلَا تَأْكُلُونَ

matches.label: A divine messenger announces a son's birth and gives his name
matches.note: wə-hinnēh ḇēn lə-śārâ ʾištekā; lam-môʿēḏ ʾāšûḇ ʾēleḵā kā-ʿēṯ ḥayyâ û-lə-śārâ ḇēn vs. wa-bashsharūhu bi-ghulāmin ʿalīm. Genesis promises a son to Sarah with a set time; the Quran gives the good news to Abraham of 'a knowing boy', with no time and no name.

passages.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר שׁ֣וֹב אָשׁ֤וּב אֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ כָּעֵ֣ת חַיָּ֔ה וְהִנֵּה בֵ֖ן לְשָׂרָ֣ה אִשְׁתֶּ֑ךָ וְשָׂרָ֥ה שֹׁמַ֛עַת פֶּ֥תַח הָאֹ֖הֶל וְה֥וּא אַחֲרָֽיו
הֲיִפָּלֵ֥א מֵיְהוָ֖ה דָּבָ֑ר לַמּוֹעֵ֞ד אָשׁ֥וּב אֵלֶ֛יךָ כָּעֵ֥ת חַיָּ֖ה וּלְשָׂרָ֥ה בֵֽן

leads.title: Psalm 50 - God summons heaven and earth; do I eat the flesh of bulls ↔ The sky expanding, all things in pairs, 'flee to God', and jinn and humans created to worship
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: God does not need sacrifices: 'If I were hungry I would not tell you... Do I eat the flesh of bulls or drink the blood of goats?' (weight 5.8). Pair score 5.8.

Only in Psalm 50 - God summons heaven and earth; do I eat the flesh of bulls: Superscription ascribes the psalm to Asaph; Every beast of the forest is mine, the cattle on a thousand hills, and the ziz of the field; God's faithful ones made a covenant with him by sacrifice; Our God comes and is not silent; fire devours before him and a tempest rages around him; Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty, God shines forth (hofia); 'I kept silent, and you thought I was one like yourself'; An oath invoking God by a repeated triple title (El, Elohim, YHWH); Whether God is in need and humans rich [contrast between the texts]; Offer to God a sacrifice of thanksgiving (todah) and pay your vows to Elyon; God rebukes the wicked who recites his statutes and covenant yet consorts with thieves and adulterers; Poet summons heaven and earth to listen; Wonder done 'so that you may know that the earth belongs to YHWH'; and 4 more.

Only in The sky expanding, all things in pairs, 'flee to God', and jinn and humans created to worship: Of everything God created pairs (zawjayn); 'So flee to God; I am to you a clear warner from him'; God created jinn and humans only to worship him; he wants no provision or food from them; The wrongdoers have a portion (dhanub, a bucketful) of punishment like that of their fellows; Fleeing from God, or to God [divergence between the texts]; Whether God, or the gods, eat the offerings [contrast between the texts]; What God created humans, or his people, for [divergence between the texts]; God built the sky with might (bi-aydin) and is expanding it (inna la-musi'un); God made the earth a cradle (mahd) or bed and laid out paths in it; No messenger came to earlier peoples without being called 'a sorcerer or a madman', as if they had bequeathed the charge to one another; God alone stretches out the heavens.
